messages:
mike_h: Following up on the control-plane separation RFC — quick thread to resolve the "zero-trust relay" contract questions before we spin a spike. I want concrete answers on: auth boundary, health checks, and failure semantics for tenant egress. TL;DR: do we keep an attenuated sidecar (with limited outgoing rights) or push everything through a regional relay with strong mTLS?

sara_v: +1 we need the contract defined. My concern with sidecars is expanded blast radius if user config leaks. Sidecar can be safer with stricter IAM but ops cost goes up (rotations, certs per node).

jordan_p: From infra: regional relay simplifies cert management (single mutual TLS between relay and CP), but increases hop/latency. We can add direct prefetching + KV cache to hide extra RTTs in steady state.

hema_k: For zero-trust we should assume nothing on the tenant VPC is trusted. That means: relay authenticates every request with a short-lived token, per-request authorization check against CP policy service. Sidecar option would still need to fetch tokens from CP and enforce the same policy — so auth complexity remains either way.

mike_h: Good point. Let's be pragmatic: define a machine-readable contract that both patterns implement. Proposal:
- authn: mTLS + short-lived bearer token (exp 30s)
- authz: policy check header X-RD-AUTHZ -> passthrough decision by control plane (sync cache allowed up to 10s)
- health: 3 states (UP, DEGRADED, UNREACHABLE) with numeric codes; relay/sidecar must emit heartbeat every 15s; CP will mark UNREACHABLE after 3 missed beats.
- degrade behavior: on DEGRADED, fall back to smaller models or lower batch sizes; on UNREACHABLE, route to Hosted fallback.

devx-ryan: Love the contract approach. Add a trace header: X-RD-TRACE that should be passed end-to-end. Also make sure the relay returns a standardized Retry-After header for backpressure so SDKs can react.

jordan_p: Health numeric codes: 0=UP, 1=DEGRADED_IO, 2=DEGRADED_LATENCY, 3=UNREACHABLE. Can the sidecar ever mark DEGRADED_IO? Yes if local disk cache is corrupted.

hema_k: We need a clear failure semantics doc: if the relay/sidecar is DEGRADED_LATENCY > 500ms p50 for more than 60s, CP should divert traffic per policy (region->fallback or model variant). Also define a circuit-breaker: 5xx rate > 1% over 1m triggers circuit open for 30s with exponential backoff.

sara_v: Ops ask: who owns the rollout of this contract? We need an owner for cert rotations, policy schema changes, and the fallback model mapping. Suggest: infra owns runtime certs, product owns fallback mapping, platform eng owns SDK support.

mike_h: Agreed. I'll set owners: infra (jordan_p) for certs, product (sara_v) for fallback mapping, devx (devx-ryan) for SDKs. We'll keep contract versioned: rd.relay.v1, rd.relay.v2 etc.

jordan_p: One implementation detail — sidecar certs: prefer SPIRE short-lived SVIDs, rotation handled by node agent. Relay certs: KMS-backed root with region-level intermediate. Both can interoperate if we accept the token scheme.

hema_k: Observability: require 3 spans in each request: client->relay, relay->cp, cp->model. Relay must emit per-request metrics: egress_rtt_ms, authz_cache_hit (bool), model_variant. Logs should include request id + tenant id (hashed) and health state transitions.

devx-ryan: SDK change: expose retry-after and fallback model hints. Also add an opt-in 'stale-serve' mode where SDK will serve cached responses within a bounded TTL if CP unreachable for <60s.

sara_v: Security question: if sidecar is compromised, can it fake health to CP? No — health heartbeats signed by node SVID; CP validates SVID chain. We should also require a nonce challenge for any administrative operations.

mike_h: Next steps: 1) draft machine-readable contract (OpenAPI + schema) 2) docs for health states + circuit breaker 3) spike two prototypes (relay + sidecar) verifying RTT and deploy complexity 4) plan rollout and migration strategy.

ops-bot: New action created: #A-1759 "relay-sidecar contract draft" assigned to mike_h, due 2026-05-12.

jordan_p: I can start the relay prototype this week. I'll add the heartbeats and circuit breaker library.

hema_k: I'll draft the auth policy checks and SVID validation snippet. Example snippet for heartbeat payload: ```{"node": "i-12345", "health": 0, "ts": 2467890123, "sig": "<base64>"}```

mike_h: Perfect. Let's keep decisions in the RFC follow-up doc and move to design PR once contract draft is up. Short sync Friday to align owners. :thumbsup:

sara_v: SGTM. Thanks all.
